div.head: Nor Grið Line 1
div.ab: [1] ⁊ on Norðhymbra lage is sanctus Petrus
And on Norðhymbra lage is sanctus Petrus

Und im Northumbrer-Recht beträgt [Busse für Verletzung von] Kirchenfrieden des H. Petrus und des H. Wilfrid und des H. Johann innerhalb der Kirchenmauern 3 ‘Hundert’ beim lebend [gebliebenen verletzten] Menschen, und bei getödtetem [ist die That durch Geld] unabbüssbar.

1. And in Northumbrian law [the compensation for breach of] the church-peace of St Peter and of St Wilfrid and of St John within the church walls is 3 ‘hundreds’ for a person [injured but] still living, and for one killed [the deed is] beyond compensation [by money].
And according to the law of the Northumbrians,
div.note: MS G (Cotton Nero A I, f. 96v, after VIII Atr. 5.2, hand c. 1070). Liebermann numbers this text by manuscript line (1–9), as the sheet does; erasure, wear and chemicals have made it partly illegible, and the bracketed letters are his supplements (with readings from G. F. Warner, 1902). Clause 1 runs over lines 1–5. The churches are York Minster, Ripon and Beverley; Wilfrid died 709, John 721; 1 ‘hundred’ of silver = 8 pounds. Liebermann dates the text c. 1015–c. 1050 and compares VIII Atr 1.1, 4 and 4.1. Column K is one line of the MS per row; Liebermann's German and the English are given on the row where each clause begins.; T: corrected against Rabin, DOML 66 (2020), p. 32 (before: ‘And on Norðhymbra lage is sanctus Petrus cyricfrið and sanctus Wilfriðus and sanctus lohannes binnan cyricwagum þreo hundred æt cwicum men, and æt dædum botleas.’); AZ: corrected against Rabin p. 32 / 33, October 2026 (was “Rabin’s 1 covers the rows Line 1, 2, 3, 4; it is given here, in the first. |; Lie bermann,; ∅”, now “∅; Liebermann,; | Saint Peter’s, Saint Wilfrid’s, and within the walls of Saint John’s: The three churches specified are those at York, Ripon, and Beverly. | Saint John’s . . . compensated: “John’s,” “hundred,” and “cannot be compensated” are all reconstructed.”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “c.1015–c.1050; post–1023 (Wormald); ?1014 (Rabin)”, now “c.1015–c.1050 (Liebermann); after 1023 (Wormald); ?1014 (Rabin)”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “c.1015–c.1050 (Liebermann); after 1023 (Wormald); ?1014 (Rabin)”, now “c.1015–c.1050 (Liebermann, I p. 473); after 1023 (Wormald); ?1014 (Rabin)”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “G 473; German 473”; 9 rows of Nor Grið); V: page of the modern editor’s text / translation, checked against Rabin (translation on the facing page), October 2026 (e.g. was “32”, now “32 / 33”; 9 rows of Nor Grið)

Manuscripts: G = London, British Library, Cotton MS Nero A.i, fol. 96v. Due to an ill-advised attempt by Liebermann to restore a difficult passage in the manuscript using a solution of sulfuric acid, much of the page on which this text appears is now unreadable. Accordingly, editions must now rely heavily on Liebermann’s initial transcription and subsequent reconstruction of illegible words.
Due to damage to the manuscript, this text is based on that found in Liebermann, Die Gesetze der Angelsachsen. Words that have been restored based on Liebermann’s notes are indicated below.
Saint Peter’s, Saint Wilfrid’s, and within the walls of Saint John’s: The three churches specified are those at York, Ripon, and Beverly.
Saint John’s . . . compensated: “John’s,” “hundred,” and “cannot be compensated” are all reconstructed.

note.seg: Petrus ist Patron zu York, Wilfrid zu Ripon, Johann zu Beverley
Peter is the patron at York, Wilfrid at Ripon, John at Beverley
mit VIII Atr. lautet gleich I Cn. 2, 3. 3. 3a
reads the same as I Cn. 2, 3. 3. 3a, together with VIII Atr.
Vgl. Gl Hundert 6; busslos 5b; Halbverletzung 3. Drei Hundert = 24 £ büsst, wer Kirchenfrieden verletzt im Umkreise einer Meile von der Kirche Ripon oder Beverley
Cf. Gl Hundert 6; busslos 5b; Halbverletzung 3. Three hundreds = 24 £ is the compensation paid by anyone who breaks the church-peace within a radius of one mile from the church of Ripon or Beverley

vgl. Grið 13. Die Unterscheidung, ob Verletzter lebt, fehlt den sonst feiner differenzirten Sonderschutz-Ansprüchen jener drei Dome seit Anfang 12. Jhs., wo als boteles (Hist. of York ed. Raine III 34), Nordisch botalaus (Alured Beverlac. in Raine’s Sanctuar. Dunelm. 1837 p. XV), vielmehr gilt die Verletzung des Asyl verleihenden friðstol, der in Beverley und Hexham noch existirt

cf. Grið 13. The distinction as to whether the injured person survives is absent from the otherwise more finely differentiated claims to special protection made by those three minsters from the beginning of the 12th cent., where what counts as boteles (Hist. of York ed. Raine III 34), Norse botalaus (Alured Beverlac. in Raine’s Sanctuar. Dunelm. 1837 p. XV), is rather the violation of the friðstol conferring asylum, which still exists at Beverley and Hexham
